subtype: Approach: relying on caffeine and energy drinks [Pitfall]
passage: Dhruv, you asked why my results dipped in October, and I'll be honest: it was the chai and the cans. I'd finish my last cup of strong tea at nine at night and open an energy drink at ten, because I had chapters left and didn't want to lose the night. It worked for about two hours. My eyes were wide, my hands slightly jittery, and I felt clever. Then at one in the morning I lay there wired and tired at the same time. Next day I was so drained I needed two more teas before first period. The plan was making tomorrow's me pay for tonight's me. I'm Sunaina, and I've switched to water, and to stopping earlier.

qa.q: What did Sunaina drink at ten at night?
qa.a: Sunaina opened an energy drink at ten.

qa.q: How did Sunaina feel at one in the morning, and what does it show?
qa.a: Sunaina felt wired and tired at the same time, which shows the drinks only masked the tiredness.

qa.q: What could Sunaina do instead to stay alert in the evening, and why?
qa.a: Sunaina could take a short break and finish the hardest topics earlier in the day, because rest helps focus more than strong drinks and does not delay sleep.

qa.q: How might Dhruv see the dip in Sunaina's results?
qa.a: Dhruv probably wondered what went wrong, and hearing the honest answer may help Dhruv avoid the same trap.

grounding: To stay alert, the student drinks strong tea and energy drinks late in the day, which masks tiredness briefly but delays sleep, so the next day starts even more drained.

subtype: Approach: relying on caffeine and energy drinks [Pitfall]
passage:
My name's Hrithik, and I share a room with my cousin Karthik in our hostel. This term I noticed something new on his desk every evening: a tall can of energy drink, sometimes two, next to a steel glass of strong tea.

"Keeps me sharp," he said, when I asked. He'd drink them around seven or eight, then study till late.

But he wasn't sharp. He'd lie in bed till two, tossing, the light from his phone on the ceiling. At six, when the bell went, he'd groan and pull the pillow over his head.

In the mornings he looked grey. By lunch he was buying another can. Once in class he put his head down and our teacher had to call his name twice.

I don't know exactly what was going on inside him. But the cans kept multiplying, and he seemed more tired every week.

qa.q: What did Hrithik notice on Karthik's desk every evening?
qa.a: A tall can of energy drink, sometimes two, next to a steel glass of strong tea.

qa.q: What might Karthik have been feeling when he groaned at the six o'clock bell?
qa.a: He was probably exhausted and frustrated, still tired after lying awake till two.

qa.q: What would you change first in Karthik's routine?
qa.a: Stop the drinks in the evening and try an earlier wind-down, since the late caffeine seems to be what keeps him awake till two.

qa.q: How does Karthik's routine look to Hrithik?
qa.a: To Hrithik it looks like a loop that makes things worse: the drinks promise alertness, but Karthik seems more drained every week.

grounding: An observer describes a student drinking strong tea and energy drinks late to stay alert, which delays sleep and leaves each day more drained.

subtype: Approach: relying on caffeine and energy drinks [Pitfall]
passage:
Tuesday, first week of board prep: Irawati bought two cans of energy drink on the way home from coaching and drank the second at nine. "Now I can do four more chapters," she told her friend Neelam on the phone. At two she was still awake, reading the same page.

Wednesday: She woke at seven feeling like wet sand. Strong tea at breakfast, another at eleven, an energy drink at four. In the evening her heart felt jittery and she couldn't sit still. Sleep came at half past two.

The next Monday: Neelam found her asleep on the library table at lunch. "You look worse than before you started all this," Neelam said gently. Irawati rubbed her eyes and counted on her fingers: four late nights, four tired days. "They're not giving me energy," she said slowly. "They're borrowing it from tomorrow."

qa.q: How many cans did Irawati buy on Tuesday?
qa.a: She bought two cans of energy drink on the way home from coaching.

qa.q: How did Irawati feel on Wednesday evening?
qa.a: She felt jittery and restless, unable to sit still, on top of being very tired.

qa.q: What else could Irawati try to stay alert without late caffeine?
qa.a: She could keep tea to the morning and take a short walk or nap early in the afternoon, so she is not borrowing energy from the night.

qa.q: How might Neelam see Irawati's week?
qa.a: Neelam probably feels worried and caring, noticing that Irawati looks worse than before and pointing it out gently.

grounding: Shows a student using strong tea and energy drinks late in the day to stay alert, which delays sleep so each next day starts more drained.
